newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's SRC has enough stocks during shutdown.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's SRC has enough stocks during shutdown.

text.p: Singapore Refining Co (SRC) said it has enough stocks to meet the needs of its shareholders during the unscheduled one-week shutdown of its 60,000-barrels-per-day crude unit which started October 1.

"During the period of shutdown, stock inventories of products will be maintained at levels to enable the refinery to meet the needs of our three shareholders," JJ Rinck, chief executive officer of SRC said in a statement.
SRC is 40 percent owned by Singapore Petroleum Co, with the remaining stakes divided equally between British Petroleum and Caltex--a joint venture between Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
The company said in the statement that the crude unit was shutdown as "part of SRC's optimisation programme to make sure that all refining units are performing to achieve maximum output."
Its two other units are operating as usual, refining a total of of 225,000-bpd of crude.
